veranderings.voor: met hulle in die graf gesit
veranderings.na: met hulle in hul grafte gesit
veranderings.rede: The subject is plural (earlier pharaohs), so the singular 'die graf' reads as one shared grave; 'hul grafte' matches the plural.

veranderings.voor: maar nie almal vir farao's nie
veranderings.na: maar nie almal was vir farao's nie
veranderings.rede: The elliptical clause lacks a verb and reads clipped; adding 'was' makes it a complete, natural clause for Grade 5.

veranderings.voor: voorwerpe gevind met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun).
veranderings.na: voorwerpe met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun) gevind.
veranderings.rede: Afrikaans places the past participle at the end of the clause; 'gevind met die naam van' is English word order. Protected names stay intact.

veranderings.voor: Sy graf het nog niemand gevind nie.
veranderings.na: Maar sy graf was nog nie gevind nie.
veranderings.rede: With the object first, a child can read it as 'his grave had not yet found anyone'; the passive is unambiguous and fits the past narrative.
'Hul' is the usual written possessive form; 'hulle' as possessive is more spoken.

veranderings.na: Daarom het rowers die graf gemis
veranderings.rede: The nearest antecedent of 'dit' is 'ingang', not the grave; naming the grave makes the reference clear and matches the lesson title.
